tip: Dismissing something: σιγά τα λάχανα (sigha ta lakhana = easy on the cabbages) = big deal / no biggie.
Botching something: τα κάνω θάλασσα (ta kano thalassa = I make them sea) = to mess up badly.
Family traits: το μήλο κάτω απ' τη μηλιά θα πέσει (to milo kato ap' ti milia tha pesi) = the apple will fall under its tree – Greek's 'apple doesn't fall far'.
Caution after harm: φυσάει και το γιαούρτι (fisai ke to yaurti = he blows even on the yogurt) = once burned.
On family bonds: το αίμα νερό δεν γίνεται (to ema nero dhen yinete = blood does not turn into water).
Cluelessness: έχω μαύρα μεσάνυχτα (ekho mavra mesanikhta = I have black midnight) = to have no idea.
Feigning ignorance: κάνω την πάπια (kano tin papia = I play the duck) = pretend not to know.
Exaggerating: κάνω τη μύγα βόδι (kano ti migha vodhi = make the fly an ox) = to blow out of proportion.
Overlooking: κάνω τα στραβά μάτια (kano ta strava matia = make the crooked eyes) = turn a blind eye.
Compromising: βάζω νερό στο κρασί μου (vazo nero sto krasi mu = I put water in my wine) = to give ground.
Romantic rejection: τρώω χυλόπιτα (troo khilopita = I eat a noodle-pie) = to be turned down.
Effort that backfires: πήγε για μαλλί και βγήκε κουρεμένος (piye ya mali ke vyike kuremenos) = he went for wool and came out shorn – hoping to gain, he lost instead.
Wasted advice: στου κουφού την πόρτα όσο θέλεις βρόντα (stu kufu tin porta oso thelis vronta) = knock all you want at the deaf man's door – Greek's 'talking to a wall'.
Patience pays: αγάλι αγάλι γίνεται η αγουρίδα μέλι (aghali aghali yinete i aghuridha meli) = little by little the sour grape becomes honey – slow progress still ripens.
Thrift: φασούλι το φασούλι γεμίζει το σακούλι (fasuli to fasuli yemizi to sakuli) = bean by bean the sack fills up – and the rhyme makes it stick.
Distance forgets: μάτια που δεν βλέπονται, γρήγορα λησμονιούνται (matia pu dhen vleponte, ghrighora lismoniunte = eyes that don't meet are soon forgotten).
Left disappointed: μένω στα κρύα του λουτρού (meno sta kria tu lutru = left in the cold bath) = left high and dry.
Steeling oneself: κάνω την καρδιά μου πέτρα (kano tin kardhia mu petra = I make my heart stone) = to harden up.
Fixation: τρώω κόλλημα (troo kolima = I eat a sticking) = to become obsessed with something.
Long grudge: κρατάω μανιάτικο (kratao maniatiko = I keep it Maniot-style) = to nurse a lasting grudge.
Staying alert: έχω το νου μου (ekho to nu mu = I keep my mind) = to keep watch / stay alert.
Total certainty: κόβω το κεφάλι μου (kovo to kefali mu = I cut off my head) = I'm absolutely sure.
Making sense of: βγάζω άκρη (vghazo akri = I get an edge) = to sort out / figure out.
Blame-shifting: φωνάζει ο κλέφτης να φοβηθεί ο νοικοκύρης (fonazi o kleftis na fovithi o nikokiris) = the thief shouts to scare the householder – the guilty accuse first.
Getting cocky: καβαλάω το καλάμι (kavalao to kalami = I mount the reed) = to become arrogant.
Being shrewd: μου κόβει το μάτι (mu kovi to mati = my eye cuts) = to be perceptive/canny.
Too many bosses: όπου λαλούν πολλοί κοκόροι, αργεί να ξημερώσει (opu lalun poli kokori, aryi na ximerosi) = where many roosters crow, dawn comes late.
On meddling: όποιος ανακατεύεται με τα πίτουρα, τον τρώνε οι κότες (opios anakatevete me ta pitura, ton trone i kotes) = whoever meddles with the bran gets eaten by the hens.
Better safe: κάλλιο γαϊδουρόδενε παρά γαϊδουρογύρευε (kalio ghaidhurodhene para ghaidhuroyireve) = better tie your donkey than go looking for it – prevention beats searching.
Sour grapes, Greek style: όσα δεν φτάνει η αλεπού τα κάνει κρεμαστάρια (osa dhen ftani i alepu ta kani kremastaria) – grapes she can't reach, the fox calls hung-up-to-keep.
